Senses.Explanation: The records define straight mind against bends, twists, crookedness, and falseness: ‘straight mind means without bends or twists.’ Literally, a straight or straightforward mind. The term is attested. The corpus supplies two compact definitions: 'straight mind means without bends or twists' (直心者，無委曲故), and 'straight mind is the site of the Way because it has no falseness' (直心是道場，無虛假故). The Platform Record repeats 'straight mind is the site; straight mind is the clean land' (直心是道場，直心是淨土), then contrasts inwardly acting crookedly while verbally speaking straight with actually carrying out straight mind. Its positive clause is 'only carry out straight mind; regarding all things, have no grasping' (但行直心，於一切法上，無有執著). Another address expands the pattern into four coordinated expressions: 'straight mind is the site; straight speech is the subtle teaching; straight conduct is subtle conduct; straight verification is the subtle result' (直心是道場，直說是妙法，直行是妙行，直證是妙果). The common collocation 'straight mind and straight conduct' (直心直行) is attested. One record describes it by the absence of self-versus-other, right-versus-wrong, falseness, and crookedness; another uses 'straight mind, straight conduct, original color, original share' (直心直行，本色本分) to characterize a named Chan figure's meetings with people.

Senses.Explanation: Chan records make this action a lineage banner for Bodhidharma’s coming while also turning it into a question and a claim that teachers qualify in their own words. Dahui Zonggao twice states the Bodhidharma formula and glosses direct pointing as what every person already has. Huitang Zuxin and Yuanwu Keqin place it in lineage discourse, while Yuanwu also says the branching lineage has no destination outside it. An unnamed monastic asks Juelang Daosheng what the paired formula means. Mengan Siyue compares it to an antelope hanging by its horns, resisting a flat explanatory capture. The evidence supports the recurring banner and its public testing without treating Bodhidharma as the grammatical speaker whenever he is named.

Senses.Explanation: Turn the light around and shine back directs attention away from outward pursuit and back toward what is present.
